howItWorks.title: How TerraNex Works
howItWorks.subtitle: A transparent 3-step decision flow connecting farm data to reliable agricultural recommendations.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Provide soil nutrient metrics (N-P-K), pH, and climate data, or capture a clear photo of plant foliage.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Our Random Forest classifier and two-stage CNN gatekeeper screen inputs against verified agronomic patterns.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Access clear crop viability rankings with APMC price metrics, or disease management advice with strict safety guidelines.

features.title: Comprehensive Agricultural Intelligence
features.subtitle: Built specifically to solve core agricultural challenges faced by Indian farmers and extension workers.
features.f1Desc: Multiclass Random Forest model evaluating 22 crops based on soil nutrients and local weather conditions.
features.f2Desc: CNN pipeline with Stage 1 foliar species verification to prevent cross-crop false alarms and unnecessary sprays.
features.f3Desc: Actionable agronomic guidance, cultural controls, and preventative steps tailored to verified plant diagnoses.
features.f4Desc: Persistent records of all crop and disease analyses to track farm health and seasonal performance over time.
features.f5Desc: Interface localized in English, Tamil, and Hindi to ensure accessibility across linguistic farming communities.

leafCompare.title: Healthy vs. Diseased Foliage
leafCompare.subtitle: Catching plant stress early prevents crop loss. Compare typical healthy foliage with infected leaf patterns.
leafCompare.healthyDesc: Vigorous green pigmentation, smooth lamina, uniform venation, and absent chlorosis or necrosis.
leafCompare.diseasedDesc: Dark water-soaked angular lesions with yellow halos, leading to defoliation and fruit sunscald if unaddressed.
leafCompare.diseasedAdvice: Screening Advice: Sanitize tools, avoid overhead spray
leafCompare.disclaimer: Illustrative diagnostic comparison. Always verify field anomalies using TerraNex leaf screening.

impact.title: Real-World Agronomic Impact
impact.subtitle: Science-backed decision support designed to promote long-term soil health, crop health, and resource efficiency.
impact.card1Desc: Matching crops to actual soil nutrient reserves and rainfall patterns reduces seed failure and optimizes fertilizer utilization.
impact.card2Desc: Identifying foliar pathogens at initial lesion onset allows cultural sanitation before entire fields require emergency spraying.
impact.card3Desc: Preventing cross-species false alarms and unconfirmed fungicide applications protects soil biodiversity and reduces input expenses.
impact.qualification: Outcomes depend on local agro-climatic conditions, farming practices, and field management.

Potato - Late blight.about: Late blight is a destructive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans that affects potato foliage and tubers under cool, humid conditions.
treatment: Remove and safely destroy heavily infected leaves and plants.
Avoid overhead irrigation and keep foliage as dry as possible.
Consult a certified local extension officer before applying any targeted fungicide.
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing and hill aeration.
Scout fields weekly during cool, overcast, and rainy periods.

Potato - Early blight.about: Early blight is caused by Alternaria solani, producing brown to black target-board concentric lesions primarily on older potato foliage.
treatment: Prune and dispose of severely infected lower leaves.
Maintain consistent soil moisture and avoid water stress.
Seek agronomist guidance for appropriate preventative protective sprays.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.
Incorporate or remove crop debris following harvest.
Maintain balanced nitrogen and potassium fertilization.

Tomato - Late blight.about: Late blight is a rapidly spreading water-mold pathogen that damages tomato leaves, stems, and fruit during cool, wet weather.
treatment: Promptly prune and bag infected plant material; do not compost.
Apply approved protective copper or targeted fungicides upon early confirmed detection.
Water at ground level and maximize ventilation in greenhouses.
prevention: Plant resistant tomato varieties where adapted.
Maintain wide plant spacing and stake/trellis vines.
Mulch around plant bases to prevent soil splash onto foliage.

Tomato - Early blight.about: Early blight causes dark concentric rings and collar rot on tomato foliage, leading to extensive premature leaf loss.
treatment: Prune affected lower leaves to improve air circulation.
Avoid overhead watering and apply water at root level.
Apply recommended protective copper fungicide sprays if spread threatens crop.
prevention: Rotate fields away from solanaceous crops for 2-3 years.
Stake plants and maintain adequate row spacing.
Apply clean organic mulch around crop base.

Pepper bell - Bacterial spot.about: Bacterial leaf spot causes water-soaked lesions that turn brown with yellow halos, leading to severe defoliation and fruit lesions.
treatment: Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet to prevent pathogen dispersal.
Prune and safely destroy infected leaves.
Apply registered copper-based bactericides in accordance with extension recommendations.
prevention: Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.
Rotate fields with non-solanaceous crops for at least two years.
